newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi refinery receives first cargo of raw sugar.
newsitem.headline: Saudi refinery receives first cargo of raw sugar.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's new sugar refinery in Jeddah has received its first cargo of raw sugar, paving the way for the kingdom's first locally-processed white supplies.

"We received the first ship of 15,000 tonnes of sugar from Australia this week and we expect to receive another one in two weeks of 40,000 tonnes," United Sugar Co's executive general manager Mohammad Kashgari told Reuters by telephone from the Red Sea port city of Jeddah.
The ship arrived on Saturday, he said.
"The first one will be used for commissioning and the second will be used for commercial production," he added.

Australia's Queensland Sugar Corp is supplying the two cargoes to the refinery, which is 51 percent owned by Savola -- Saudi Arabia's biggest food group, 15 percent by Britain's Tate and Lyle and the rest by Saudi sugar trading firms.

"We are starting commissioning our refinery later this month. Once that is done we will begin commercial production," Kashgari said of the 500,000 tonne annual capacity plant. --Hilary Gush, Dubai newsroom +9714-626990
